What was generalizable here: this wasn't a method error — I had the right table, right row, right scaling (already in millions), right operation (sum the 12 monthly cells). I was off by exactly 100, which is the signature of a single-cell transcription error: one month's value read 100 too low. The durable lesson is a verification protocol — when a 12-cell sum is off by a clean round number, exactly one cell is wrong by that amount, so cross-check the sum against an in-document calendar-year total and hunt the misread cell rather than re-checking arithmetic.

I added:
- references/monthly-sum-transcription-verify.md — the full protocol (list all 12 cells labeled, cross-check vs in-doc annual control total, re-read suspect digit-place, re-add via script).
- A one-line pointer in SKILL.md so it surfaces for "sum of all individual calendar months in <YEAR>" questions.
